news.title: Jasmine Crockett torched for honoring singer with notorious history of violence: 'Completely vile'
news.text: Rep. Jasmine Crockett, D-Texas, who recently lost her Senate bid, is facing online backlash after she honored music artist Chris Brown by entering him into the congressional record this past weekend. "Now, y’all know, I tend to get in trouble every once in a while. I’m a make this real quick. I need to know who run it! So is Dallas in the building?" Crockett said as she took the stage alongside Brown on Saturday evening. "Let’s give it up for Chris Brown," she added to applause from the audience. The moment drew scrutiny from viewers online, raising questions about Crockett’s status as a lawmaker and whether it should be used to celebrate Brown, someone with a history of domestic violence. AMERICA OWES BLACK WOMEN 'EVERYTHING,' REP JASMINE CROCKETT RANTS OVER JULY 4 WEEKEND Among other instances of misconduct, Brown pleaded guilty in 2009 to felony assault after he attacked his then-girlfriend and famous singer, Rihanna. Many images of her injuries were made public, sparking intense condemnation from the music industry. His violence, however, wouldn’t stop there. He was involved in a 2013 altercation with Frank Ocean, another singer, and pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor assault charge that same year. In 2017, another ex-girlfriend was granted a domestic violence restraining order against him after she alleged physical abuse. Most recently, Brown pleaded guilty to charges of striking producer Abe Diaw twice in the head with a glass tequila bottle in July 2023. He is expected to receive a sentence in October for a separate charge for affray, a criminal charge in English law for unlawfully threatening violence against another person. Andrew Kerr, an investigative reporter with the Washington Free Beacon, quickly noted Brown’s past in a post to X after news of Crockett’s tribute began to spread online. "Kamala Harris-endorsed Rep. Jasmine Crockett uses her congressional authority to honor Chris Brown, the rapper best known for beating ever-living s--- out of Rihanna in 2009," Kerr wrote. Shannon Watts, a Democratic activist and political commentator, also pointed out Brown’s storied past. WATCH: HEARING TURMOIL AS JASMINE CROCKETT UNLOADS ON MLK'S NIECE IN WILD RACIALLY-CHARGED RANT "Chris Brown pled guilty to felony assault after brutally attacking Rihanna. Another ex, Karrueche Tran, later obtained a five-year restraining order after testifying that he abused and threatened her. He has also faced multiple allegations of violence and sexual assault against other women," Watts wrote. Crockett’s member statement, a form of recognition that lawmakers can have entered into the congressional record without any vote, recognizes "the artistry of Chris Brown and Usher Raymond." On stage on Saturday, Crockett framed her member statement as a way to recognize two key artists who had helped shape contemporary R&B and pop music, especially for the Black community. "I know it’s almost Sunday, so I wanna be clear. Weeping may endure for a night, but joy comes in the morning. And right now, we are experiencing Black joy to the highest level, and I wanted to make sure we document that in the Congressional Record," Crockett said. But Democratic strategist Ameshia Cross believes that the moment was a political miscalculation, coming across as ignorant of the challenges in the Black community. "Chris Brown has a problem, and several folks beyond Rihanna have met his violent rage. It’s well-documented. This was a ridiculous move by Crockett," she wrote on X. "Also, when Black women suffer [domestic violence] at the highest rates and often fatally, this was tone deaf as hell," she added. Eric Michael Garcia, the D.C. bureau chief of the Independent, echoed Cross’ thinking. "Absolutely disgusting to see Jasmine Crockett platform and honor an abuser of women. Just completely vile," Garcia wrote in a post of his own. Dan Winslow, a New York Times bestselling author, hinted that the moment had changed his view of her. WATCH: TALARICO EMBRACES ‘FREAKY’ IDENTITY AS CROWDS CHANT NAME MEANT AS INSULT: ‘SO WEIRD’ "CHRIS BROWN plead guilty to beating Rihanna. It was a horrific and savage beating. Crockett thought he deserved to be honored. Absolutely disgusting behavior. I am glad she lost. I will never support her again," Winslow wrote. In response to the public backlash, Brown posted a response to his Instagram account, pleading to be left alone and expressing displeasure at Crockett having put him in the spotlight. "Funny thing is... YALL CAME TO ME WITH THIS! NOT THE OTHER WAY AROUND. I was minding my own d-mn business. My shows in Dallas were already sold out. I ain't asked to be honored because I knew some sh-t like this would happen... I have an idea how about y'all leave me the f--- alone and let me focus on the fans that spent their money to actually see and support me," Brown wrote. news.title: Trump, 80, Keeps Repeating the Same Unhinged Story
news.text:
Donald Trump has dug up his bonkers old shark tale. 

The 80-year-old president was speaking about new executive orders on hunting and fishing at an event in the Rose Garden on Thursday when he stumbled onto an old favorite. 

He said he had been speaking with a mid-size ship manufacturer and asked them what the biggest challenge they faced with electric boats. 

“He said, ‘The weight is enormous. We can barely carry that much weight,’ because, you know, electric is a much heavier form of propulsion, and they said the weight is enormous. 

“I said, ‘Let me ask you a question. If you get a little leak and the water starts coming in your boat and you’re in—do you get electrocuted or not?’ 

“He said, ‘You know, nobody’s ever asked me that question.’ And I said, ‘So here’s my question...’ You remember this? I used to say it during the campaign, driving the press crazy, but people found it sort of amusing. 

“I said, ‘So if I’m in an electric boat and I see them going down and the water’s pouring in, so I know I’m going to be electrocuted, but five yards away there are sharks, do I take the electrocution or do I go swimming with the sharks?’ And you know what my answer was? I’ll take the electrocution, OK? I’ll take the electrocution—but he didn’t know how to answer the question. He said, ‘No idea.’”

He left people dumbfounded with the same question many times before, in 2023 and 2024. 

Multiple times on the trail, he said he had asked a South Carolina boat manufacturer a question in September 2023: If the boat sinks, would the people onboard be electrocuted?

Each time, he said the manufacturer said they had never been asked that question before. It also came with the same caveat: that if passengers jumped, they would be eaten by sharks. 

“The [boat’s] battery is now underwater and there’s a shark that’s approximately 10 yards over there, by the way, a lot of shark attacks lately,” he said to a Las Vegas audience in June 2024. 

He said he asked the businessman: “Do I get electrocuted… or do I jump over by the shark and not get electrocuted? Because I will tell you, he did not know the answer.”

Again, he revealed that the man said that “No one has ever asked me that question.”

He said it for the first time in October 2023, in Iowa, one month after the supposed interaction with the businessman. “You know what I’m going to take? Electrocution,” he mused that time around. “I will take electrocution every single time.”

He said it again in Houston in the following month, in November. “I said, ‘What would happen if you’re out at sea and your boat sinks and you have a whole big electric deal under you—would you get electrocuted?’ He said, ‘You know, nobody’s ever asked me that question.’” That time, he had been talking about the Army wanting to build electric tanks before going off on a tangent. 

Trump was panned by the media for his use of the story, which he pushed back on in June 2024 on the campaign trail, saying, “It’s actually not crazy. It’s sort of a smart story, right?”

He was clearly satisfied with this conclusion and did it again in Grand Rapids, Michigan, the following month. 

“If there’s a shark about 10 yards away, do I get electrocuted or do I go with the shark?… because I will take electrocution all day long.” It was his first time doing a rally alongside future Vice President JD Vance. 

“The Washington Post is a pathetic institution no longer worth the paper it’s printed on, and they should be embarrassed for wasting time writing a story about boats sinking when our country is sinking from Joe Biden and Kamala Harris’s failed leadership,” then-Trump campaign spokesperson Karoline Leavitt told the Post in a statement in July 2024.

It wasn’t the only mystifying riff he went on during Thursday’s Rose Garden speech. Continuing his aquatic theme, he got himself in a terrible muddle trying to talk about duck hunters. 

“And we also strongly support your duck hunters,” he said. “The duck hunter hunters thing is a big deal. 

“And they came to us and they met with my people and they came to me, my people, and, uh, we are fully in favor of our duck hunters. Who would think that’s a big deal? 

“But I, I hear I got 100 percent of the duck hunters vote, right? What did they get there? 100? If there was 150, I would have gotten 150 percent. I mean, the competition wasn’t that tough.”

As for sharks, Trump’s never liked them. “Sorry folks, I’m just not a fan of sharks,” he said on Twitter in 2013. “And don’t worry, they will be around long after we are gone.”
news.summary:
Photo Illustration by Elizabeth Brockway/The Daily Beast/GettyDonald Trump has dug up his bonkers old shark tale. 

The 80-year-old president was speaking about new executive orders on hunting and fishing at an event in the Rose Garden on Thursday when he stumbled onto an old favorite. 

On the campaign trail, the then-Republican nominee developed a taste for a nonsensical story about battery-powered boats and sharks, and more than two years later he stood in the White House and reprised it once more. 

Read more at The Daily Beast.
